title: console: the header connection chip never shows a mid-session outage — after the first successful connect no failed request moves the adapter's connection state, so a stopped backend leaves stale data on screen with no indicator
body:
Filing-gate category ① (product defect, named landing point) and ③ — the maintainer's order in the dispatching session, verbatim: 「测试遇到的问题，可以提交issue」.

QA-source: objectstack-ai/objectstack#23104 · platform-core.console-installability-indicators · C2

**Reader who acts:** the objectui `domain:ui` execution seat (`app-shell` header, `data-objectstack` adapter). **Dedupe:** semantic issue search on this repo, closed included, "connection status chip hidden when backend goes down mid-session reconnecting error state never shown after initial connect" — 0 hits.

## Environment

objectstack `36b2889c` with the console built from objectui `1fb1ced36243` (the pin hop of objectstack-ai/objectstack#23104, since landed as `f451a5964`), stock `examples/app-showcase`, admin persona. Reproduced on two fresh full stop-and-restart runs plus an emulated-failure run (every `/api/**` request aborted); mechanism confirmed in source by the PM seat; not a regression of the pin hop (no hop commit touches `ConnectionStatus.tsx`, `AppHeader.tsx` or the adapter's `index.ts`).

## Reproduction

1. Boot the showcase, sign in, open an app surface (e.g. the Tasks grid). The chip shows "Connected" (seen at ~0.8 s) and hides by ~2.9 s — the 2000 ms auto-hide, correct.
2. Stop the backend process mid-session.
3. Poll the page every 0.5 s for 20 s for any connection wording (Connected / Reconnecting / Disconnected / Connection error / Offline / Failed / Error): nothing appears. The grid keeps showing stale rows while background requests (`GET /api/v1/data/sys_inbox_message`, `GET /api/v1/approvals/requests`) fail `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`.

**Expected:** a prominent, persistent reconnecting / error state for as long as the backend is unreachable. **Control:** the same poller sees "Connected" on load and "Offline" under the browser's offline emulation, so it does read the header.

## Mechanism (objectui `1fb1ced36243`)

`packages/app-shell/src/layout/AppHeader.tsx` renders `ConnectionStatus` from the adapter's `ConnectionState`. In `packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts` every `setConnectionState(...)` call (`connecting`, `connected`, `error`, `reconnecting`) sits inside `connect()` — the initial discovery. Once that has succeeded, a failed data request never moves the state, so a mid-session outage is invisible.
